answer: Each account becomes a vertex in a crystal lattice, and weekly it must emit a pulse: a short puzzle answer tied to a random public event from the past hour, so pre-recorded bots cannot replay it. A vertex keeps its place only if its pulses arrive on time and its neighbours, real people met in the lattice, confirm the answers look human. Sybil clusters betray themselves because their vertices link only to each other, forming a dense crystal with no outside edges, which the lattice prunes. Honest users just pulse weekly; a farm must fake thousands of live, timely, human-confirmed pulses.
